grand_strategy.reading: Timor-Leste is a small, young state whose money is an oil fund spent faster than it grows, and whose one large asset is a gas field across a sea border settled in 2018 that it still cannot turn into revenue. Its foreign policy is a small state's hedging: Indonesia is the market and the former occupier, Australia the paymaster with an open grievance over the 2004 spying case, China the source of finance it has mostly not signed for, and Portugal the language and identity it shares with the CPLP. ASEAN membership (October 2025) is the frame that makes it a regional state rather than a dependent one, and the bet is Greater Sunrise: if Canberra pays for a pipeline to the south coast, the gas becomes a bridge out of the fund; if it waits past the fund, Dili has no second currency.

stances.note: Partner, with the 1975-99 occupation and the 1999 referendum violence underneath (bond grievance). What holds the relation is trade and the border: about 70% of goods on the market are Indonesian-origin (Trade Minister Budi Santoso, 2025), bilateral trade reached US$391.3m in 2024, the land-boundary talks were pushed in Oct 2024, and a 21-year-old border trade pact is being revised. Indonesia backed the ASEAN bid and Prabowo signed the admission declaration on 26 Oct 2025. Trend warming because the 2024-26 steps run one way. Not an ally: nothing in the sources is a security alignment.

stances.note: Partner with a grievance. Australia's bugging of Dili's cabinet during the 2004 Timor Sea talks (the Witness K case, alleged) has not been apologised for: the charges against Bernard Collaery were dropped in July 2022, which Dili welcomed, but Canberra has not admitted the operation and no 2025 apology was found (HRLC, Jan 2024). The Albanese visit of 28-29 Jan 2026 produced a joint declaration, 'a new partnership for a new era': US$220m for human development, US$80m for private-sector development, US$8.2m for ASEAN and WTO participation, a 10% share of combined future upstream Greater Sunrise revenue to a Timor-Leste infrastructure fund (other reporting gives a larger share; not resolved here), and 10,000 Timorese workers in Australia by 2027-28. The friction is the field: Dili wants a pipeline to its south coast, Woodside prefers Darwin, and first gas has slipped to 2034-35. Grade partner rather than reluctant partner because the cooperation is broad and no source calls it grudging; trend stable because the declaration and the slipping gas talks pull in opposite directions.

stances.note: Kin: language and the colonial past. Timor-Leste opened its first embassy abroad in Lisbon on 5 July 2002. Portugal's four-year framework of EUR 75m (EUR 5m more than the last) is centred on education and the teaching of Portuguese (announced in 2025). Inside the CPLP, Timor-Leste, Portugal and Brazil opposed Equatorial Guinea's bid for the 2027-29 presidency, which the PALOP countries back; Timor-Leste was elected to a temporary CPLP presidency in Dec 2025 and its president led the CPLP mission to Bissau after the Nov 2025 coup. Partner, not ally: broad cooperation without a security alignment, and the impasse is still open (Aug 2026).
